title: Canonical transport of represented raw classes through a commutative square
statement: Let f:X→Y, f′:X′→Y′, g:Y′→Y and g′:X′→X form a commutative square of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let U→Y be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put U′=U×_Y Y′ [def-pc-fibre-product] and let A_U be the free abelian sheaf represented by U [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. Inverse-image composition [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] and the free represented pullback comparison give a canonical isomorphism ρ:g′*f*A_U≅f′*A_U′. For q≥0 and a raw derived-Hom class z:f*A_U[0]→F[0][q] in the bounded-below derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], construct its pullback as the single of ρ⁻¹, the inverse exact inverse-image/single comparison, D⁺g′*(z), its q-shift comparison, and the shifted single comparison at F. This is a construction using exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], with no choice of a cohomology representative. The cached evaluation of a shifted raw class after an exact functor L and a left exact section functor R applies H⁰(RL) to the class, evaluates at the inverse degree-zero comparison of the chosen section, then applies the specified q-shift comparison [def-sbc-raw-restricted-cohomology-comparison-map]. This is the explicit evaluation formula, not an existence choice. These transport and evaluation constructions are bundled additive group morphisms. Exact derived inverse image is additive, and precomposition and postcomposition are additive, so transport preserves zero and sums. The point formulae identify these bundled morphisms with the stated raw class operations. The native raw comparison is exactly bundled evaluation at the represented identity generator; its definitional equation is cached in the evaluation API.

proof.text: Adjunction, the free abelian adjunction, sheafification and Yoneda identify Hom(g*A_U,B) naturally with B(U′). The representing isomorphism identifies g*A_U with A_U′. Compose its f′ inverse image with the inverse sheaf square comparison to obtain ρ.

Use exact inverse image on bounded-below derived categories. Insert its canonical single and shift comparisons and precompose with the single of ρ inverse. Each factor is a specified morphism, so the displayed composite constructs the pulled-back raw class.
The cached point evaluation is the composite of inverse degree-zero comparison, H⁰ of the mapped class and the target shift comparison. Its formula theorem is reflexivity.

Additivity of the derived functor and bilinearity of composition show that exact transport preserves zero and sums. Use these proved laws to construct its additive group morphism. Evaluation is already an additive morphism from the derived-Hom group. Their application formulae are reflexivity. Unfold the cached bundled evaluation: the native raw comparison is the same evaluation map followed by the same shift comparison, so reflexivity gives its presentation equation.

    {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {g' : X' ⟶ X} (sq : CommSq g' f' f g)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (q : ℕ) (U : Y.Etale)
    (z : (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
      (((f)^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).obj ((abelianComparisonFree Y).obj U)) ⟶
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F)⟦(q : ℤ)⟧) :
    (DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
      (((f')^*[AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}]).obj
        ((abelianComparisonFree Y').obj (g.Etale.obj U))) ⟶
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
